adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:81 — No test asserts the `check` exit code (0 in testCompatible, 3 in testWrongVersions at :96/:105), so the RECREATE 4->3 renumbering the scripting contract depends on stays unverified and could regress without any test failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes exit-code constants in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and adds `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, `testCompatible` asserts `exitCode()` only for the metadata subcommand, and `testWrongVersions` only asserts error output for the `check` subcommand runs (no `exitCode()` assertions). So the renumbered recreate/compatibility exit-code contract is not verified by these tests and could regress without test failure.

Also, there is no analogous “feature not enabled” test path for `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` (all `check` invocations in this diff add `ENABLE_FEATURE`). This leaves the new gating/exit-code behavior in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` only partially exercised by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/compatibility/CompatibilityResult.java:35 — FEATURE_DISABLED reuses exit code 4, which the code previously returned for "recreate required", so old automation will read a check that never ran as a valid recreate verdict instead of a failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` in `CompatibilityResult.java`. So exit code `4` is now repurposed from “recreate required” (old behavior) to “feature disabled” (new behavior). While not an internal correctness bug in the new code (it deliberately avoids clashing with picocli’s 1/2 codes and documents `m|4` as feature-disabled), it is a diff-grounded backward-compatibility/contract change that could confuse existing automation that previously interpreted exit code 4 as “recreate required”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 — The template appends `--features=rolling-updates` on the CLI, which overrides any `features` set in keycloak.conf or KC_FEATURES; this contradicts the guide's "include all configuration options" rule, and metadata/check then run on a different feature set than the deployed server.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `updatecompatibility` docs template to always run `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ... --features=rolling-updates` (docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc). In the same PR, the update-compatibility subcommands now hard-fail unless `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is enabled (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata). Hardcoding `--features=rolling-updates` in the template effectively bypasses that gating for the command invocation, so the docs-generated command may run with a different feature set than what the user has configured elsewhere. Whether this "overrides" keycloak.conf/KC_FEATURES isn’t provable from the diff alone, but the unconditional forcing of the feature in the template is diff-grounded and a concrete documentation/usage concern rather than a runtime code defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc:448 — The docs say the Operator will fail without `rolling-updates`, but this change adds no enforcement in operator/src/main, and UpgradeTest always enables the feature (plus the Dockerfile bakes it in), so a missing operator gate can never be caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds documentation warnings that the Operator will fail unless the preview feature `rolling-updates` is enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc) and adds CLI enforcement for update-compatibility commands, but it does not show any corresponding enforcement in `operator/src/main` (only `UpgradeTest` is changed to always enable the feature via `FeatureSpec`, and the custom-image Dockerfile bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the build). This creates a diff-grounded concern that the Operator-side requirement is only documented/assumed and is not validated or testable within the Operator code shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image:5 — The test image bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the build to match the CR's build-time features, but the docs never tell users with optimized custom images that they must rebuild with the feature before setting spec.update.

The docs changes added cautions about enabling the `rolling-updates` preview feature (e.g., in `advanced-configuration.adoc` and `update-compatibility.adoc`) and updated CLI examples to pass `--features=rolling-updates`, but they do not mention rebuilding optimized/custom images with the feature enabled before using rolling updates. This is a concrete documentation gap tied to the new build-time flag, not a runtime defect shown in the diff.

This PR diff does not show any corresponding updates to CLI help/feature list approval snapshots (if such snapshot tests exist), so a reviewer concern about needing to update those artifacts is plausible, but the diff alone does not prove those tests are present or will fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 — The shared macro appends a hardcoded `--features=rolling-updates` after the user's parameters, which conflicts with or overrides a user's own `--features` (the guide says to pass the exact start config); `features` is also build-time, so the flag may not take effect on an optimized image (the author had to bake it into Dockerfile-custom-image).

This is a concrete, diff-grounded documentation/macro design issue and could lead to duplicate/overriding `--features` flags if `${parameters}` already includes one, but the exact runtime behavior (override vs error) is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:132 — The exit-code table describes 4 as "Rolling Upgrade is not possible", but 4 is a precondition failure (feature disabled) that `metadata` also returns, so scripts may read it as a compatibility verdict meaning "recreate".

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows exit code 4 is now used for a precondition/usage failure when the preview feature is not enabled: both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata early-exit via `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` after printing “Unable to use this command...” (and `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). The docs table in `docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc` adds row `m|4` but phrases it as “Rolling Upgrade is not possible... feature disabled”, which can be read like a compatibility verdict rather than “command could not run due to missing feature flag.” This is a documentation/UX clarity issue grounded in the diff, not a demonstrable behavioral defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — Tests never assert the renumbered exit codes (3 for recreate in the incompatible test, 4 for feature-disabled), and the feature-disabled test only covers `metadata`, not `check`, so the scripted exit-code contract is not pinned by tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the CLI exit-code contract in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and adds `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`), and adds feature-gating that calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`. In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and launches `UpdateCompatibility` with `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` (not `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`), and none of the existing incompatible-path tests assert the exit codes (e.g., no assertion for recreate=3, feature-disabled=4). This is a concrete gap in coverage for the newly introduced/changed exit-code behavior, not a runtime defect shown by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error text, never the new FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit code, and the `check` subcommand's feature gate is not exercised at all

However, the new `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text (`cliResult.assertError(...)`) and does not assert the exit code, so it would still pass if the command printed the message but exited with a different code (e.g., 0/1). adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:61 — testMissingOptionOnSave only asserts absence of "Missing required argument", so it passes even without ENABLE_FEATURE (the command would exit early with the feature-disabled error), proving nothing about the flag enabling the command.

Even though the @Launch includes `ENABLE_FEATURE`, this assertion would also pass if the command exited early due to the new feature-disabled guard (error message would be different but still not contain "Missing required argument"). So the test does not actually verify that `--features=rolling-updates` enabled the command path; it’s a specific weakness in the new/modified test rather than a product bug.

UpdateCompatibilityMetadata ...)` asserts `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`, but the subsequent `distribution.run(... UpdateCompatibilityCheck ...)` only asserts output (`"[OK] Rolling Upgrade is available."`) and absence of an error message, without asserting the exit code is `CompatibilityResult.ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (0). adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:44 — All positive tests enable the feature via a runtime --features flag; no test covers the build-time-enabled path (kc.sh build --features=rolling-updates, then an optimized run) that the operator Dockerfile-custom-image now relies on.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, the newly added positive-path invocations all pass `--features=rolling-updates` at runtime (e.g., `@Launch({..., ENABLE_FEATURE})` and `distribution.run(..., ENABLE_FEATURE)`), and a new negative test asserts failure when the flag is absent. Separately, the operator’s `Dockerfile-custom-image` was changed to enable the feature at build time via `kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`. The diff shows no test exercising the build-time-enabled/optimized-run scenario (build with the feature, then run the commands without the runtime flag), which is a concrete coverage gap for the operator’s intended usage, but not a proven functional defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:105 — createInitialDeployment returns early for the null strategy, so rolling-updates is enabled only for RECREATE, and no operator test covers the documented failure when an update strategy is set without the feature.

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff for `createInitialDeployment`, `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` is executed unconditionally (after null-check/initialization of `FeatureSpec`) and is not tied to `RECREATE`. The alleged “early return for the null strategy” is not present in the provided diff hunk, so the claim that rolling-updates is enabled only for RECREATE (and that the method returns early) cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java:115 — setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replaces any features already enabled on the base test CR with an immutable list instead of appending.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpgradeTest#createInitialDeployment`, the diff unconditionally does `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`. This clearly overwrites any pre-existing enabled feature list on `FeatureSpec` (if it was already populated) rather than appending, and `List.of(...)` is immutable, which could be problematic if later test code expects to modify the list in-place. The diff does not show any existing enabled features being set before this, so it’s not a verifiable functional break, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern.
